summary.text: 老 is a pictograph interpreted as an aged, bent person with long hair leaning on a staff. Its common meaning is “old” or “aged”; the earliest cited oracle-bone use is a place name and does not attest that meaning.

formation.text: Pictographic: the oracle form is interpreted as a bent, long-haired person holding a staff. A later dictionary analysis instead parses 人、毛、匕 and explains the graph through whitening hair; it does not confirm the origin of the earlier form.

components.text: The whole graph depicts a bent person with long hair and a staff. One paleographic analysis identifies 人 and 毛 as the person and hair, and 丨 as the staff; bronze forms render the staff in a 匕-like shape. These parts describe the picture, not a proven sequence of substitutions.

history.text: The staff appears as 丨 in the oracle-form analysis and as 匕 in bronze forms; it is sometimes written 止. Later upper-part variation is also reported, with 由 possibly serving as a phonetic element in one Spring and Autumn variant. This does not establish 由 as part of the original formation.

uncertainties.text: The earliest cited oracle-bone instance is a place name, with no established link to the meaning “old” and no absolute date supplied. The reported bronze and Warring States uses do not establish a complete chronology.

The later dictionary analysis parses 人、毛、匕; Duan Yucai offers a different analysis of the seal form, deriving it from 毛匕 without treating 人 as a separate element. Neither confirms the oracle graph’s formation.

senses.text: The earliest cited oracle-bone instance uses 老 as a place name; it attests that use, not the lexical meaning “old.”

senses.period: bronze inscriptions; absolute dates not supplied here
senses.text: Reported bronze examples use 老 for an elderly person and as an adjective meaning “old.”

senses.gloss: father, written with 老 for 考
senses.period: bronze inscriptions; absolute dates not supplied here
senses.text: Bronze examples reportedly use 老 to write 考 “father.” Whether this was a semantic development or a writing substitution is unresolved.
The common current meaning is “old” or “aged.”
“Experienced” is also recorded as a current sense; its development is undated here.

limitations.text: The place-name, elderly-person, adjective, and father uses do not establish a chronological semantic chain. The reciprocal gloss of 老 and 考 and the traditional 轉注 account are historical interpretations, not proof of how these senses developed.

overview.text: 老 pictures a bent, long-haired person with a staff. It commonly means “old” or “aged”; its earliest cited oracle-bone use is a place name, not evidence for that meaning.

components.text: Read the whole graph as a picture of a bent person with long hair and a staff; the staff’s written shape varies in later forms.
